247. Liberation War of Lafrarosa (3)
For a moment, it seemed as though the desert had been split in two.

The Red Plutonian fleet, which had been focusing on the meteor shower, had no choice but to be taken aback once again. The red protective shield split at the impact of the golden blade of the torrent, producing a terrible screeching sound.
Ships were exploding.
Ordinarily, they might have held out a bit longer, but the crew vomited dark blood as the chaos entered through the broken shields.
“K-hack!”
“Cough…!”

The chaos swallowed the crew in the blink of an eye. While the ship's captains of the Red Plutonian managed to push back the chaos to some extent, they couldn't withstand the impact of the Sky Splitter attack.
No matter how advanced their ships were, in such circumstances, proper operation was impossible. Their pride in high-performance equipment and devices was turning into useless objects.

With each surge of golden blades from the battlefield, about a dozen ships were destroyed. The fire and smoke spread by the exploding ships covered the sky, and the Sky Splitter attack repeatedly erased their presence.
“Today, the death of our Dreck brother feels particularly sorrowful…”
Shimat narrowed his eyes as he spoke.
Drek's Hon.
Before Shimat's awakening as a Battle God, the poor decisions of the great warriors had sadly led to Dreck's meaningless death.
If Dreck had been alive, even sending just him into Tikan or the Garden of Swords would have made it impossible for the alliance to fight as actively as they are now.
However, what's done is done.
“Open the bridge. Bakarun, Rakiman, Bekios. Both the Great Battle Kings and all direct first-class Battle Kings, prepare to join the battle.”
Shimat made a different decision than before.
He ordered the entire strongest force of the Red Plutonian, except for the Battle God fortress 'Kri', to participate in the battle directly.
It might have been more advantageous to fight safely from inside the fortress, especially in a situation where the battlefield is covered with chaos.
It was just a hunch.

Shimat felt an intuition that if they couldn't stop the alliance this time, Lafrarosa would be safely liberated. With the witch also intervening, the already unpredictable situation would only become more complicated.
Suddenly! Woong...!
Except for the Patlok, all air fortresses opened their bridges. The moment Shimat and the three Great Battle Kings appeared, the Battle Kings of the Blue Plutonian grinned
"Good, those lowly creatures are finally jumping out of the air fortress."
"Jin brothers, let us handle the rest. You trample with Murakan those lowly creatures Battle God."

The mages of Zipfel had given up on entering the battlefield upon the meteor shower. Initially, even if they were phantom or white night, there was no way to participate in this battle without a figure like Elona.
Originally, Zipfel sent them not for combat but for information gathering. They had simply made the safest choice since they were relatively the slowest.
However, the giants on the battlefield wouldn't even allow them to observe their fight.
Jin stepped out and looked up at Shimat, who was standing on the spreading wave energy as if it were solid ground.
The atmosphere was different from usual.
Not just cool and solid, but an aura of grandeur unique to an ancient loser was emanating.
The gaze only one who once ruled the world could have.
Jin intended to ensure he never opened those eyes again.
"You seem to know chaos well, Jin Runcandel. Seeing that you gave up the main base as soon as chaos spread in the desert."
"I know well. I've won many battles."
Shimat's eyes and heart were shining red.
He, too, was gauging Jin's power, not just the force obtained by reaching Genesis rank, but also the inexplicable power of Jin Runcandel as a person.
A will that only someone who has transcended fate several times could possess.
Looking back, even before Jin ascended to Genesis rank, he always exuded that aura. No matter who the opponent was, no matter how strong, no matter how overwhelming the difference.
He shone his eyes as if he could stand against them and win.

"Since before I regained my memory as a Battle God, your attitude always made me uneasy. Back then, I was First-class Battle King Shimat. But now... I cannot tolerate it. Because of beings like you, we seek the Sun God. Escape from predetermined fate? That might be a pleasant thing for an individual, but essentially, it's an act that corrupts the world's order."
Whooosh...!
The blade of the Sun Sword, Tetalon, blazed fiercely. Behind him, the amplifying vibrations from the power source of the air fortress Pibil, which stood tall as a mountain, continued.
That vibration was merging the land of the desert, torn apart by Jin’s sword, back into one. The remaining power of the Sky Splitter, regardless of Jin's will, sank into the ground that it had split.
He suppressed it with sheer power. The difference in firepower was still vast. However, that was only when comparing just Jin alone.
[A non-god talking about order? Even a god, if they blurt out such nonsense like you, a slightly stronger mortal, they can meet their end.]

Murakan, behind Jin, spread his two pairs of wings and spoke. His massive black dragon frame might seem like just a mere beast compared to the airborne fortress, but the inherent power within him wasn't.
A spiritual aura rising like mist softly wrapped around Jin and Murakan. Even the main cannons of the airborne fortress seemed unable to easily disperse this mist.
[Moreover, if you want to speak of order, shouldn't you have stayed away from chaos? Are you going to say the pure spirit of the witch spreading across the desert has nothing to do with you?]
“The path to order is inevitably filled with chaos, Black Dragon Murakan. In the end, it's the shape of the world that is realized at the end that matters."
Only the result matters.
That was also a core belief of the Red Plutonian. Therefore, they classified their kin by rank, and they didn't hesitate when their peers were sacrificed for a purpose.

Because they believed that once a 'perfect world' arrives, all past mistakes and errors would be rectified. And this notion was not exclusive to the enemy tribe but was a commonality among all forces, except for the Vamel Alliance.

“I've met many who speak like you, Shimat. Some died by my hand, and some still survive and fight against me. They all have one thing in common: their plans were thwarted by meeting me. Just like you."
“You have a knack for speaking about uncertain matters as if they’ve already occurred."
“Yes, because I can see it. Your future."
Jin and Shimat simultaneously swung their swords.

When the golden lightning and red wave energy clashed, a bright white explosion and shockwave occurred between them. Even before that shockwave disappeared, Jin, together with Murakan, rushed forward and thrust his sword into Shimat's chest.
The dense red wave energy slowed down Jin's sword. Yet it was still quick, seemingly just a flash of light. However, Shimat had already shifted his position and slashed at Murakan's wing.

The blade seemed to smoothly pass through as if cutting through a shadow, and Murakan lashed out with his front claws at that moment. Yet again, the red waves of the airborne fortress froze his claws in place.
All airborne fortresses, except for Patlok, were assisting Shimat like this. It was as if he was protected by three impenetrable shields.
Jin and Murakan quickly switched their attack and defense, fending off Shimat's counterattacks, and decided to target the airborne fortress first.

They thought they could create at least a small gap by stopping at least one of them. Instead of targeting the closest Pibil to Shimat, it would be better to target the ones on the left and right, Rital and Bessel.

'The Demon Trio isn't participating in the battle. They probably have something to do with the chaos, but relying on them is just a temporary advantage. In the end, we must face Shimat and the airborne fortresses with the power of the alliance alone.'
Unlike the two who constantly had to avoid the Red Plutonian waves, Shimat was continuously swinging Tetallon, utilizing those waves as if they were a path.

The condensed red wave energy on the Divine Sword, Tetallon, had already struck close to Jin and Murakan several times. Every impact point was always followed by the main canons of the air fortresses.
This meant that even a single strike would result in severe injuries. Murakan might not know, but for Jin, who didn't possess as much endurance and healing power, it was especially more lethal.
Black Dragon's Ultimate Move
Dark Arrival
The moment Murakan released his spiritual energy, a massive darkness began descending over the battlefield, which was already filled with clashing energies and dazzling lights.

The darkness swiftly enveloped the protective barrier of the aerial fortress and then tore apart in all directions. The red protective layer attached to the spiritual energy tore apart too, and Murakan immediately lunged towards it.

If Rital was alone, that strike would have shattered several layers of its outer armor. However, Murakan was pushed back by the concentrated fire from Pibil and Bessel, forcing him to regain his stance.
Meanwhile, Jin swiftly passed by Shimat and thrust his sword into the lower part of Rital. This had been the strategy Jin and Murakan had been aiming for from the beginning.
The blade piercing through the armor triggered an internal explosion of a massive lightning strike. This explosion, albeit weak, affected even the heart and power of Rital.
As a result, the red wave energy emitted by Rital momentarily disappeared, and Murakan's dragon breath struck Rital again. Rital was slammed into the ground like a nail.
This was the result of Shimat not protecting Rital. At that time, Shimat, accepting minor damage to Rital, was reaching out with the Red Sky God Sword towards Lafrarosa's dimensional gate.
He judged that striking Lafrarosa would be more effective.
Jin also had to make a decision. Whether to continue attacking the momentarily vulnerable Rital or to protect Lafrarosa.
Jin instantly chose the former. If he ambiguously tried to protect Lafrarosa, he would inevitably be dragged around by the Red Plutonian.
Zwooosh-!
Jin descended like thunder and plunged Sigmund into the very center of Retal's upper part. He then executed a rush attack.

From inside Retal, golden rays, like thorns, began to pour out. Despite the massive size of the fortress and the massive blow it sustained, its form did not completely collapse, but it was evident that it was the most significant damage since the fortress's first appearance.
'My brothers will hold on. Focusing only on Shimat and the aerial fortress is better for them too…'
That's when Jin saw it.
Shimat was rapidly falling from a crack in his vision. It was a sight completely opposite to what Jin had anticipated, expecting another thrust of the Red Sky Divine Sword.
The reason Shimat retreated from Lafrarosa's dimensional gate was none other than the sudden emergence of Vahn's sword energy, similar to before.
